sentences.text: WOMAN: I've been meaning to ask you for some advice about restaurants.
sentences.zh: 我一直想请教你一些关于餐厅的建议。

sentences.text: I need to book somewhere to celebrate my sister's 30th birthday, and I liked the sound of that place you went to for your mum's 50th.
sentences.zh: 我需要预订一个地方来庆祝我姐姐的30岁生日，而你之前为你妈妈50岁生日去的那家餐厅听起来不错。

sentences.text: MAN: The Junction.
sentences.zh: The Junction 餐厅。

sentences.text: Yeah, I'd definitely recommend that for a special occasion.
sentences.zh: 对，这种特殊场合我肯定推荐那家。

sentences.text: We had a great time there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那儿过得特别开心。

sentences.text: Everyone really enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 大家都很喜欢。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Where is it again?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那家店到底在哪儿？

sentences.text: I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我想不起来了。

sentences.text: MAN: It on Grayson Street only about a two walk from the station
sentences.zh: MAN: 它在格雷森街上，离车站步行只要大约两分钟。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh that's good I prefer not to have to drive anywhere but I don't want to have to walk too far either.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，那太好了。我宁愿不开车去任何地方，但也不想走太远。

sentences.text: MAN: Yes, the location's perfect, but that's not necessarily why I'd recommend it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，位置确实很好，但这不是我推荐它的主要原因。

sentences.text: The food's amazing.
sentences.zh: 菜特别棒。

sentences.text: If you like fish, it's probably the best restaurant in town for that.
sentences.zh: 要是你喜欢鱼，它大概是城里吃鱼的最好的餐厅。

sentences.text: It's always really fresh and there are lots of interesting dishes to choose from But all the food is good there
sentences.zh: 那里的食材总是非常新鲜，而且有大量有趣的菜品可供选择，不过所有食物都很美味。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Is it really expensive?
sentences.zh: 是不是很贵？

sentences.text: MAN: It's certainly not cheap, but for a special occasion I think it's fine It's got a great atmosphere and before dinner you can go up on the roof and have a drink It's really nice up there, but you need to book It's very popular as the views are spectacular.
sentences.zh: MAN: 价格当然不便宜，但既然是特殊场合，我觉得完全可以接受。那里氛围很棒，而且晚餐前你可以上到屋顶喝一杯，那儿真的很棒，不过得提前预订，因为那里非常受欢迎，视野也极为壮观。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Sounds good.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 听起来不错。

sentences.text: So that's definitely a possibility then.
sentences.zh: 那这肯定是一个可以考虑的选择。

sentences.text: Is there anywhere else you can think of?
sentences.zh: 你还能想到别的地方吗？

sentences.text: MAN: If you want somewhere a bit less formal, then you could try Paloma.
sentences.zh: MAN: 如果你想找个稍微不那么正式的地方，也可以试试帕洛玛餐厅。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Where's that?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那家店在哪儿？

sentences.text: I haven't heard of it.
sentences.zh: 我从来没听说过。

sentences.text: MAN: No, it's quite new.
sentences.zh: 对，它挺新的。

sentences.text: It's only been open a few months, but it's got a great reputation already.
sentences.zh: 才开业几个月，但口碑已经很好了。

sentences.text: It's in a really beautiful old building on Bow Street.
sentences.zh: 在 Bow 街上的一栋很漂亮的老建筑里。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh, I think I know where you mean.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，我想我知道你说的是哪家了。

sentences.text: Right beside the cinema.
sentences.zh: 就在电影院旁边。

sentences.text: MAN: Yes, that's it.
sentences.zh: 对，就是那儿。

sentences.text: I've only been there a couple of times, but I was really impressed.
sentences.zh: 我只去过几次，但印象特别深。

sentences.text: The chef used to work at Don Felipe's, apparently.
sentences.zh: 据说主厨以前在 Don Felipe's 工作。

sentences.text: I was really sorry when that closed down.
sentences.zh: 它关门的时候我挺遗憾的。

sentences.text: WOMAN: So is all the food they serve Spanish, then?
sentences.zh: 那他们供应的都是西班牙菜吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Yeah.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是啊。

sentences.text: You can get lots of small dishes to share, which always works really well if you're in a group.
sentences.zh: 你可以点很多小份菜肴一起分享，如果是一群人去的话，这种方式效果特别好。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Hmm.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 嗯。

sentences.text: Worth thinking about.
sentences.zh: 值得考虑一下。

sentences.text: MAN: Yeah.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是啊。

sentences.text: There's a lively atmosphere and the waiters are really friendly.
sentences.zh: 那里气氛活跃，服务员也非常友好。

sentences.text: The only thing is that you need to pay a £50 deposit to book a table.
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是订位要先付50英镑押金。

sentences.text: WOMAN: A lot of restaurants are doing that these days.
sentences.zh: 现在很多餐厅都这么做。

sentences.text: I should have a look at the menu to check if there is a good choice of vegetarian dishes.
sentences.zh: 我应该先看看菜单，确认一下素食选项是否丰富。

sentences.text: A couple of my friends have stopped eating meat
sentences.zh: 有几个朋友已经不再吃肉了。

sentences.text: MAN: Not sure I say the selection of those would be quite limited.
sentences.zh: MAN: 我不太确定，我觉得那些菜的选择范围会相当有限。

sentences.text: MAN: I've just thought of another idea.
sentences.zh: 我刚想到另一个主意。

sentences.text: Have you been to the Audley?
sentences.zh: 你去过 Audley 吗？

sentences.text: WOMAN: No, don't think I've heard of it.
sentences.zh: 没有，我好像没听说过。

sentences.text: How's it spelt?
sentences.zh: 怎么拼写？

sentences.text: MAN: A-U-D-L-E-Y.
sentences.zh: A-U-D-L-E-Y。

sentences.text: You must have heard of it.
sentences.zh: 你肯定听说过。

sentences.text: There's been a lot about it in the press.
sentences.zh: 媒体上报道过很多。

sentences.text: WOMAN: I don't tend to pay much attention to that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我通常不太关注这类消息。

sentences.text: So where is it exactly?
sentences.zh: 那它具体在哪儿？

sentences.text: MAN: It's in that hotel near Baxter Bridge, on the top floor.
sentences.zh: 在 Baxter Bridge 附近那家酒店的顶楼。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh, the views would be incredible from up there.
sentences.zh: 哦，从那儿看风景一定很棒。

sentences.text: MAN: Yeah, I'd love to go.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我很想去。

sentences.text: I can't think of the chef's name, but she was a judge on that TV cookery show recently.
sentences.zh: 我想不起主厨的名字了，不过她最近在那个美食电视节目里当过评委。

sentences.text: And she's written a couple of cookery books.
sentences.zh: 而且她还写过几本烹饪书。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh, Angela Frayne.
sentences.zh: 哦，Angela Frayne。

sentences.text: MAN: That's the one.
sentences.zh: 就是她。

sentences.text: Anyway, it had excellent reviews from all the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，所有报纸都对它给出了极佳的评价。

sentences.text: Hello and welcome.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎光临。

sentences.text: My name's Heather: McCallum and I'm one of the potters who work here at Edelman Pottery.
sentences.zh: 我叫希瑟·麦卡勒姆，是埃德曼陶艺工作室的陶艺师之一。

sentences.text: Before we go into the workshop, I just want to say a bit about the craft of pottery.
sentences.zh: 在进入工坊之前，我想先简单介绍一下陶艺这门工艺。

sentences.text: Then we'll have a look at the equipment and you can try making a pot of your own.
sentences.zh: 接着我们会参观一下设备，你们还可以亲自尝试制作一个陶器。

sentences.text: Like man: y people, I'm sure you know that pottery as an art form is tens of thousands of years old.
sentences.zh: 和许多人一样，我相信你们一定知道，陶艺作为一种艺术形式已有数万年历史。

sentences.text: And we know this because it stands the test of time.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为它经受住了时间的考验。

sentences.text: Things like baskets and pictures don't survive on the earth in the same way that pots do. and even if ancient pots are found in small pieces they still provide a lot of information about the past.
sentences.zh: 像篮子和绘画这类物品无法像陶器那样在地球上长久保存；即便古代陶器仅以碎片形式被发现，它们仍能为我们提供大量关于过去的信息。

sentences.text: There no doubt that pottery has given archaeologists a fascinating insight into how ancient hills lived The shape of an artefact may have been lost but archaeologists can tell whether the pots were for, say, storage or cooking by examining the impressions on the clay, the scratches from tools, and the clay itself can reveal where the pots came from.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，陶器为考古学家提供了深入了解古代人类生活方式的迷人视角。尽管某件器物的具体形状可能已不复存在，但考古学家仍可通过观察陶土上的印痕、工具留下的刮痕，以及陶土本身的成分，来判断这些陶器是用于储藏还是烹饪，甚至还能推断出陶器的产地。

sentences.text: When I ask people why they want to take a pottery class with me, they sometimes talk about these things.
sentences.zh: 当我询问人们为何想跟我学习陶艺课程时，他们有时会谈到这些方面。

sentences.text: Like our ancestors, they hope that something they create will also last longer than they do, that their work, whether it is good or not, might say something about humanity man: y years after their death.
sentences.zh: 正如我们的祖先一样，他们希望亲手创作的作品也能比自己存续得更久——无论作品优劣如何，都可能在自己去世多年后，向后人诉说关于人类文明的某些信息。

sentences.text: Of course, you will all have your own reasons for coming here.
sentences.zh: 当然，你们每个人来这里都有各自的理由。

sentences.text: As far as I'm concerned, what I love most is the concentration you need to make a good pot.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我最喜爱的是制作优质陶器所需的那种专注力。

sentences.text: That focus takes you away from the stresses of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这种专注能让你暂时忘却日常生活的压力。

sentences.text: If you're elderly, it's also good exercise for hands and wrists and helps with arthritis.
sentences.zh: 对老年人来说，陶艺还能锻炼手部和手腕，有助于缓解关节炎症状。

sentences.text: And of course, it's a fun activity for children because it's so messy.
sentences.zh: 当然，对儿童而言，这同样是一项充满乐趣的活动，因为过程非常‘ messy ’（混乱）。

sentences.text: Here at Edelman Pottery, we show you some of the basic pottery techniques so that you can use these to create whatever you wish.
sentences.zh: 在埃德曼陶艺工作室，我们会向你们展示一些基础陶艺技法，以便你们能运用这些技巧自由创作心仪的作品。

sentences.text: A gift for a friend, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 比如，为朋友制作一份礼物。

sentences.text: Like nearly everyone who comes here, I'm sure this is the first time you will have tried the art so we'll keep things simple today.
sentences.zh: 我相信，和几乎所有来这里的学员一样，今天将是你们首次尝试陶艺，因此我们今天的课程内容将保持简单易懂。

sentences.text: Now, before we move on, can I just say a word about what you're wearing?
sentences.zh: 现在，在我们继续之前，能否请各位注意一下自己的着装？

sentences.text: As we said in our email please remove any watches, necklaces etc and put them somewhere safe.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在电子邮件中所提醒的，请摘下所有手表、项链等饰品，并将其妥善存放。

sentences.text: If you have long hair do tie it back now.
sentences.zh: 如果你留长发，请现在就把它扎起来。

sentences.text: We provide aprons later but I trust your clothes are old but comfortable, not your favourite T-shirt or jeans.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们会提供围裙，但我相信你们穿的衣服是旧的但舒适的，而不是你们最喜欢的T恤或牛仔裤。

sentences.text: So now we're in the workshop.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到了车间。

sentences.text: Have a look around.
sentences.zh: 请四处看看。

sentences.text: There's a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多事情正在进行。

sentences.text: To make pottery that will last, you need a potter's wheel, a kiln, which is basically a very hot oven where you fire the pottery, and some tools.
sentences.zh: 要制作经久耐用的陶器，你需要一台拉坯机、一座窑炉（本质上是一种温度极高的烤箱，用于烧制陶器）以及一些工具。

sentences.text: So, first, the kiln.
sentences.zh: 那么，首先来看窑炉。

sentences.text: If you look over in the far corner, you'll see one of ours.
sentences.zh: 如果你们朝远处角落看去，就能看到我们的一座窑炉。

sentences.text: Since their invention, kilns have changed very little, though in the past 20 years a lot of progress has been made in temperature control.
sentences.zh: 自发明以来，窑炉本身变化不大，不过在过去20年里，温度控制方面取得了很大进展。

sentences.text: Basically, a kiln removes the water from clay at temperatures of around 1000 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 基本上，窑炉在约1000摄氏度的高温下将黏土中的水分彻底去除。

sentences.text: This allows anything you've made to set permanently in shape.
sentences.zh: 这使得你们所制作的任何物品都能永久定型。

sentences.text: It's a pretty ugly heavy object that's hard to keep in a house or flat, so most people don't have one.
sentences.zh: 它是一个相当笨重丑陋的物件，很难安置在家或公寓里，因此大多数人家里都没有。

sentences.text: You may think, can't I use my oven?
sentences.zh: 你们或许会想：‘我能不能用自家烤箱呢？’

sentences.text: Well, that's possible, but domestic ovens don't really get hot enough and eventually the clay will crack and fall apart.
sentences.zh: 嗯，理论上可行，但家用烤箱根本达不到所需高温，最终黏土会开裂并散架。

sentences.text: Some people fire pottery in a fire pit outside but bear in mind… that can be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 有些人会在室外的火坑中烧制陶器，但请务必注意……这可能很危险。

sentences.text: You also need to know about safety procedures for kilns as they release toxic compounds into the air.
sentences.zh: 你们还需了解窑炉的安全操作规程，因为窑炉会向空气中释放有毒化合物。

sentences.text: Every potter needs a potter's wheel.
sentences.zh: 每位陶艺师都需要一台拉坯机。

sentences.text: This machine is used to shape the clay into an object with circular walls or sides, such as a bowl.
sentences.zh: 这种机器用于将黏土塑造成具有圆形壁或侧边的器物，例如碗。

sentences.text: Its invention revolutionised the pottery industry, allowing multiple items to be produced in a day.
sentences.zh: 它的发明彻底改变了陶器行业，使人们每天能批量生产多种器物。

sentences.text: Lastly, there are a number of different tools that potters use, depending on what they want to make.
sentences.zh: 最后，陶艺师还会使用多种不同工具，具体取决于他们想要制作的器物。

sentences.text: When you start, your hands can make all kinds of shapes and curves without relying on a sculpting tool.
sentences.zh: 刚开始时，你的双手可以做出各种形状和曲线，而无需依赖雕塑工具。

sentences.text: However, there are some basic tools that you will need to handle the clay on the wheel.
sentences.zh: 然而，有一些基本工具是你在拉坯机上处理陶土时必需的。

sentences.text: Some look very strange and have even odder names that you may find hard to remember.
sentences.zh: 有些工具看起来非常奇怪，甚至有着更奇怪的名字，你可能会觉得很难记住。

sentences.text: Rather than go through them all now, I'll just name a few tools as we go along.
sentences.zh: 与其现在一一介绍所有工具，不如我们在操作过程中逐一提及几种。

sentences.text: We can provide these and I wouldn't recommend spending money on them yet.
sentences.zh: 我们可以提供这些工具，而且我目前不建议你们花钱购买。

sentences.text: So, let's try making a pot of your own.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来尝试自己制作一个陶罐吧。

sentences.text: If you sit down...
sentences.zh: 如果你坐下来……

sentences.text: TAMARA: Shall we go through the notes we've made from our research into loneliness now, Dev?
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 我们现在来梳理一下我们针对孤独感所做的研究笔记吧，Dev？

sentences.text: DEV: OK, Tamara.
sentences.zh: DEV: 好的，Tamara。

sentences.text: It's been a real eye -opener.
sentences.zh: 这真是一次令人眼界大开的经历。

sentences.text: I had no idea that loneliness has been increasing steadily for the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我完全没想到，过去20年来孤独感一直在稳步上升。

sentences.text: TAMARA: I know.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 我知道。

sentences.text: And it's the same all over the world.
sentences.zh: 而且全世界都是如此。

sentences.text: The downside of a modern lifestyle, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，这大概是现代生活方式带来的负面影响吧。

sentences.text: DEV: Did you come to any conclusions about what the reasons for the increase are?
sentences.zh: DEV: 你有没有得出关于这种增长原因的任何结论？

sentences.text: TAMARA: Well, I'd assumed it was mainly an issue for the elderly, but in fact it's something which affects young people just as much.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 嗯，我原本以为这主要是个老年人的问题，但实际上它对年轻人的影响同样严重。

sentences.text: DEV: So nothing really to do with longer lifespans.
sentences.zh: DEV: 所以这跟寿命延长其实没什么关系。

sentences.text: What about social media?
sentences.zh: 那社交媒体呢？

sentences.text: In my case, far from making me feel isolated, it actually does the opposite. it?
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，它非但没有让我感到孤立，反而起到了相反的作用，是吗？

sentences.text: TAMARA: It definitely does more good than harm.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 它带来的益处显然远大于害处。

sentences.text: I'd say loneliness has a lot to do with the way cities are designed.
sentences.zh: 我认为，孤独感与城市的设计方式有很大关系。

sentences.text: People living in high flats with not much opportunity to speak to their neighbours
sentences.zh: 住在高层公寓里的人们几乎没有机会与邻居交谈。

sentences.text: DEV: I think you right
sentences.zh: DEV: 我觉得你说得对。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Another possible reason is that people are having fewer children and don live in large extended family groups.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 另一个可能的原因是，人们的生育数量减少了，也不再生活在庞大的扩展式家庭中。

sentences.text: DEV: But in this country anyway, that all changed decades ago.
sentences.zh: DEV: 但至少在我们这个国家，这种情况几十年前就已改变了。

sentences.text: And yet loneliness is a more recent problem.
sentences.zh: 然而孤独感却是一个更为近期才出现的问题。

sentences.text: TAMARA: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 我想确实如此。

sentences.text: A more plausible explanation is that people are having to move around for work and often end up living miles away from their family and friends.
sentences.zh: 一个更可信的解释是，人们因工作需要四处奔波，结果常常住在离家人和朋友数英里远的地方。

sentences.text: DEV: That's true.
sentences.zh: DEV: 没错。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Looking at the studies on health risks and loneliness, there are claims that loneliness has as much impact as smoking 15 cigarettes a day.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 查阅关于孤独感与健康风险的研究，有观点称孤独感对健康的影响相当于每天抽15支烟。

sentences.text: DEV: Or similar to the risks caused by obesity.
sentences.zh: DEV: 或者与肥胖引发的风险相似。

sentences.text: But I'm not sure there's enough evidence for some of these claims.
sentences.zh: 但我并不确定这些说法是否有足够证据支持。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Well, what about that one in Finland, which showed that loneliness increased the risk of cancer by about 10%?
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 那么芬兰那项研究呢？它表明孤独感使患癌症的风险增加了约10%。

sentences.text: And those findings have been supported by other studies too.
sentences.zh: 而且这些发现也得到了其他研究的支持。

sentences.text: DEV: You're right about that one.
sentences.zh: DEV: 关于那项研究，你说得对。

sentences.text: I was actually thinking of the studies on dementia.
sentences.zh: 我实际上想到的是有关痴呆症的研究。

sentences.text: Some found no association between loneliness and dementia, and others found the opposite.
sentences.zh: 其中一些研究未发现孤独感与痴呆症之间存在关联，而另一些研究则得出了相反结论。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Not exactly reliable, then.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 这样看来，其可靠性就不太高了。

sentences.text: There's been a lot of research on cardiovascular disease and whether loneliness contributes to that.
sentences.zh: 目前已有大量针对心血管疾病的研究，探讨孤独感是否对其有所影响。

sentences.text: DEV: Yes, I read that it was hard to reach a judgment, as the definition of loneliness varied quite a lot, and the responses from participants were too subjective.
sentences.zh: DEV: 是的，我读到过，由于‘孤独感’的定义差异很大，且参与者反馈过于主观，因此很难得出明确结论。

sentences.text: But there's no doubt that loneliness contributes to a weakened immune system.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，孤独感会导致免疫系统功能减弱。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Unquestionably.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 这一点毋庸置疑。

sentences.text: The data on that is sound.
sentences.zh: 相关数据是可靠的。

sentences.text: DEV: What did you think about the evolutionary theory of loneliness?
sentences.zh: DEV: 你对孤独感的进化理论怎么看？

sentences.text: TAMARA: Well I thought the idea that loneliness evolved because it motivated people to be with other people is quite convincing.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 嗯，我认为‘孤独感之所以进化而来，是因为它能促使人们与他人相伴’这一观点颇具说服力。

sentences.text: Survival often depended on group cooperation.
sentences.zh: 生存往往依赖于群体协作。

sentences.text: DEV: But I don think there is enough evidence to claim that there must be a group of neurons in our brains which influence social behaviour by making us feel bad when we're alone.
sentences.zh: DEV: 但我认为，尚无足够证据断言：我们大脑中必然存在一组神经元，通过让我们独处时感到不适来影响社交行为。

sentences.text: TAMARA: There are a few studies which support the theory, but not conclusively enough.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 有一些研究支持这一理论，但证据尚不充分。

sentences.text: More evidence is needed.
sentences.zh: 还需要更多证据。

sentences.text: DEV: And anyway, this theory's not really useful when it comes to solving the problem of loneliness today.
sentences.zh: DEV: 而且，就当下解决孤独问题而言，这一理论实际上并无太大用处。

sentences.text: TAMARA: True.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 没错。

sentences.text: DEV: Should we look at the relationship between loneliness and mental health now?
sentences.zh: DEV: 我们现在是否该探讨一下孤独与心理健康之间的关系？

sentences.text: TAMARA: OK.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 好的。

sentences.text: So, loneliness and depression are clearly related and that's been recognised by various governments around the world.
sentences.zh: 孤独与抑郁症之间显然存在关联，这一点已被世界各国政府所认可。

sentences.text: But unlike depression, loneliness has no recognised clinical form.
sentences.zh: 但与抑郁症不同，孤独并未被认定为一种临床疾病。

sentences.text: DEV: There's no available diagnosis or effective treatment and that's not likely to change.
sentences.zh: DEV: 目前既无明确的诊断标准，也无有效治疗方法，而且这种情况短期内不太可能改变。

sentences.text: TAMARA: I don't think so either I was thinking we should start our presentation with an example from our own experience I like to talk about how lonely I was when I started university being away from home for the first time and all that
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 我也不这么认为。我在想，我们是否该以自身经历的一个例子作为演讲的开场？我喜欢谈谈自己刚上大学时的孤独感——那是我第一次离家求学，诸如此类的经历。

sentences.text: DEV: Good idea.
sentences.zh: DEV: 这主意不错。

sentences.text: Everyone will be able to relate to that although a lot of students were probably too embarrassed to admit to it.
sentences.zh: 大家都会对此产生共鸣，尽管许多学生可能因羞于启齿而不敢承认。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Yeah.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 是啊。

sentences.text: We could discuss ways of dealing with loneliness as well, like just talking to strangers.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以讨论一些应对孤独的方法，比如主动与陌生人交谈。

sentences.text: DEV: Loads of studies have shown that interactions with shop assistants and bar staff make people feel more optimistic and relaxed.
sentences.zh: DEV: 大量研究表明，与商店店员、酒吧服务员等人的互动能让人们感到更乐观、更放松。

sentences.text: TAMARA: I don't know about that, but it must make people feel more connected with their community.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 这一点我倒不太确定，但它肯定能让人们感觉与所在社区的联系更紧密。

sentences.text: DEV: True, although you need to be a certain kind of person to be able to just strike up a conversation.
sentences.zh: DEV: 的确如此，不过你得是某种特定性格的人，才容易主动开启对话。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Good point.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 说得对。

sentences.text: We should say something about solitude and how being alone and being lonely aren't the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我们还应提及独处（solitude）的概念，并说明独处与孤独并非同一回事。

sentences.text: It's strange the way some people can't stand being by themselves while others love it.
sentences.zh: 有些人在独处时如坐针毡，而另一些人却乐在其中，这种现象确实很奇特。

sentences.text: DEV: Yeah, the research shows a certain amount of solitude is beneficial for wellbeing, which I appreciate, but being alone isn't something I actually like.
sentences.zh: DEV: 是的，研究表明一定程度的独处对身心健康有益，这一点我认同，但独处实际上并不是我喜欢的事情。

sentences.text: I'd never choose to go on holiday alone, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，我绝不会选择独自去度假。

sentences.text: TAMARA: Me neither.
sentences.zh: TAMARA: 我也不会。

sentences.text: DEV: Well, let's not... you
sentences.zh: DEV: 好吧，我们先别……你

sentences.text: It's quite hard to think of a city that doesn't have a big river running through it.
sentences.zh: 要想到一座没有大河穿城而过的城市，其实相当困难。

sentences.text: If you think about the major cities in the world, Shanghai, New York, Mumbai, London, they're nearly all built on rivers.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想世界上那些主要城市——上海、纽约、孟买、伦敦——它们几乎全都建在河流之上。

sentences.text: When these cities were established hundreds or even thousands of years ago, the rivers were a big part of people's lives.
sentences.zh: 当这些城市在数百甚至数千年前建立时，河流曾是人们生活中极为重要的一部分。

sentences.text: In 16th century London, the quickest way to get from one part of the city to another was by river.
sentences.zh: 在16世纪的伦敦，从城市一地前往另一地最快的方式就是乘船走水路。

sentences.text: But people also used the river for fishing, as the water then was relatively clean, and they would also go on boat trips up and down the river just for pleasure, as a relaxing escape from the noise and bustle of the city streets But as industries dev: eloped and populations increased city rivers suffered The rising number of people meant there was a huge increase in the amount of sewage discharged into the rivers.
sentences.zh: 但人们也利用河流捕鱼，因为当时的河水相对洁净；人们还会纯粹为了休闲娱乐而乘船沿河上下游览，以此作为逃离城市街道喧嚣与繁忙的一种放松方式。但随着工业发展和人口增长，城市河流遭受了严重损害。人口激增导致排入河流的污水量大幅增加。

sentences.text: Rivers had always been used for this purpose, but when the number of inhabitants was so small, that wasn't such a problem.
sentences.zh: 河流一直被用于这一用途，但当居民数量极少时，这并不构成太大问题。

sentences.text: However, as cities grew to over a million inhabitants, the impact on the rivers became more serious.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着城市人口增长至百万以上，河流所承受的影响便日益严重。

sentences.text: In addition, other types of pollution increased, as factories were built beside the river and discharged their waste materials into the water.
sentences.zh: 此外，其他类型的污染也在加剧：工厂沿河而建，并将废料直接排入水中。

sentences.text: This got worse over time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况随着时间推移而愈发恶化。

sentences.text: As recently as 1957, scientists at London's Natural History Museum declared that the River Thames was dead in biological terms, as the water was too filthy to support any kind of life.
sentences.zh: 就在1957年，伦敦自然历史博物馆的科学家们还宣称，泰晤士河在生物学意义上已‘死亡’，因为河水过于污浊，无法支撑任何生命形式。

sentences.text: But in recent years, as rivers lost their industrial function, cities have begun to recognise their true value and to take steps to clean them up.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，随着河流逐渐丧失其工业功能，各城市开始重新认识到河流的真正价值，并着手开展清理工作。

sentences.text: For example, the River Thames is now cleaner than it's been for 150 years.
sentences.zh: 例如，如今泰晤士河的洁净程度已超过过去150年来的任何时期。

sentences.text: These days you can see seals swimming in the water, and recently people had to try to rescue a whale, which had got lost and swam up the river from the sea by mistake.
sentences.zh: 如今你能在水中看到海豹游弋；最近还曾有人试图营救一头迷路的鲸鱼——它误从大海游入了这条河流。

sentences.text: Unfortunately, they didn't succeed, but the problem was disorientation rather than the quality of the water.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是营救未能成功，但问题在于鲸鱼方向感迷失，而非水质不佳。

sentences.text: Then, all around the world, riverside areas are now seen as prime sites for dev: elopment.
sentences.zh: 随后，全球各地的滨河区域如今都被视为开发的黄金地段。

sentences.text: Warehouses that were once used for storing goods are now being converted into expensive restaurants and also into apartments with river views, which are in great demand and sell for astronomical prices.
sentences.zh: 昔日用于储存货物的仓库，如今正被改造成高档餐厅，以及拥有河景视野的公寓——这类公寓需求旺盛，售价高得惊人。

sentences.text: In Los Angeles, on the west coast of the USA, an architect has plans to revitalise the banks of the river and to make a park there which can provide facilities for sports as well as a natural environment for relaxing in It also hoped that the riverside can be used for other purposes It's been proposed that facilities could be provided for displaying projects related to various kinds of art that have been produced by local people, for example.
sentences.zh: 在美国西海岸的洛杉矶，一位建筑师已制定计划，旨在振兴该市河流两岸，并在此建造一座公园，既提供体育设施，又营造供人放松的自然环境。同时，人们也希望滨河区域能发挥其他功能。例如，已提议在此设置展场，用以展示当地居民创作的各类艺术作品。

sentences.text: In the city of Paris, During the summer months of July and August, all the traffic is banned from the roads by the sides of the river, and the banks are transformed into beaches, where people can relax in deck chairs under potted palm trees, sunbathe or buy a drink or a snack while enjoying the view.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎市，每年七月和八月的夏季期间，河岸道路全面禁止车辆通行，河岸则被改造为沙滩：人们可坐在盆栽棕榈树下的躺椅上休憩、日光浴，或一边欣赏风景一边购买饮品或小吃。

sentences.text: But to make the most of our rivers in our increasingly crowded cities, we need to allow them to regain their original purpose and be used as a means of transport, reclaiming our streets from cars and lorries.
sentences.zh: 但要在日益拥挤的城市中最大限度地善用我们的河流，我们必须让河流恢复其原始功能——作为交通通道，从而将街道从汽车和卡车中解放出来。

sentences.text: To do this, we'll have to shift more traffic back to the river, but this time cleanly and silently, making the most of modern technology.
sentences.zh: 为此，我们必须将更多交通流量重新引回河流，但这一次需以清洁、静音的方式实现，并充分利用现代技术。

sentences.text: Already, more than two billion passengers use the ferry to travel in cities around the world, like Istanbul, San Francisco and New York, and these numbers are set to rise further.
sentences.zh: 目前，全球已有超过20亿乘客乘坐渡轮在伊斯坦布尔、旧金山和纽约等城市出行，而这一数字还将进一步上升。

sentences.text: Admittedly, it's not a fast way of travelling, but neither is a car when it's stuck in traffic.
sentences.zh: 诚然，渡轮并非一种快速的交通方式，但当汽车陷入交通拥堵时，其速度也同样不快。

sentences.text: Of course, passenger traffic on roads might decrease as more people start working from home, but another recent dev: elopment, the huge rise in online shopping, has meant that another form of urban traffic just keeps on growing, and that's deliveries.
sentences.zh: 当然，随着越来越多的人开始居家办公，公路客运量可能会下降；但另一项近期发展——在线购物的激增——却导致另一种城市交通形式持续增长，即货物配送。

sentences.text: Trucks and vans in the city pollute and double-park while dropping off parcels.
sentences.zh: 城市中的卡车和厢式货车在运送包裹时会造成污染，并且常常在路边双排停车。

sentences.text: Imagine using the immense capacity of shipping to take these trucks off the road.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，利用航运的巨大运载能力，将这些卡车从公路上移除。

sentences.text: One freight barge can replace 44 large trucks, uses far less energy and causes less pollution When the barge docks at the riverside the parcels could be taken the last few kilometres to their final destination on cargo bikes, electric ones of course.
sentences.zh: 一艘货运驳船可替代44辆大型卡车，能耗更低，污染也更少；当驳船停靠河岸码头后，包裹可通过货运自行车（当然是电动的）完成最后几公里的配送。

sentences.text: This is already happening in the Dutch city of Amsterdam, and in future the final stage could even be carried out by drone, although at present this isn't allowed.
sentences.zh: 这已在荷兰阿姆斯特丹市付诸实践；未来，最后一段配送甚至可能由无人机完成，尽管目前尚不被允许。

sentences.text: Wouldn't it be great to unblock our city centres in this way?
sentences.zh: 以这种方式疏通我们的市中心，岂不是非常棒吗？

sentences.text: Looking further ahead...
sentences.zh: 展望更远的未来……
